answer: Bonded, work-attested reputation resists sybils. Each agent posts a stake and earns reputation only when peers verify its output over many rounds; reputation piles up like a dune, slowly, and cannot be bought. A cloned identity is hollow, with no attestation history, so its vote and reward weight stay near zero until it spends time and compute. Scaling an attack means replicating this dune-building per fake agent, and any dishonesty slashes the stake. Trust blooms like a lotus only from a verifiable record, so faking many identities costs as much as honest work, killing the sybil's edge.
